info.title: Emudoc API
info.description: Programs read and change an organisation's projects with an API key, as the member who made it. Lists come a page at a time, `next` naming where the next starts; a request that makes something may carry an Idempotency-Key; a refusal says what to do next in `detail`.

indexed just now, and what one upload may carry.

401.description: No API key, or one revoked, rolled or run out.

402.description: Never answered since the app has no plans; kept for the programs written for it.

403.description: The key's scope or its member's role does not allow it.

404.description: Nothing of this id that the key's member sees.

post.description:
Upload files into the project, as a multipart form of `files`, each indexed in the
background. The request is refused whole when it carries more files or bytes than one upload may
(413; `GET /api/v1/status` says how many); a file is refused alone, with why, for its size, for
bytes that are not the type its name says, or as a file the project holds already
(`duplicate_of`), while the others are kept. With an Idempotency-Key, the upload sent again is
given the first one's answer.

post.description:
Give the document a new file, as a multipart form of `file`, which it reads in the earlier
one's place, keeping its id and what names it; the earlier file stays as a version
to download, and its pages count again as the new one is read. Refused, with nothing changed,
for a file an upload would refuse (400, 413), for bytes the project holds already (409), and
while the document is being indexed (409; send it again once it is not). With an
Idempotency-Key, the version sent again is given the first one's answer.

post.description:
Ask a question in a chat the key's member started; the worker writes the answer, which
is followed by its id. It counts as a question asked, and is refused with 409 while the chat's
last answer is still being written and with 429 while the organisation has too many being
written at once. With an Idempotency-Key, the question sent again is given the first one's
answer, and asked and counted once.

post.description:
A document could not be read, or the malware scan quarantined it: its indexing ended, and
no other is to run after it. `data.error` says why.

Asked.title: Asked
Asked.description: A question as saved, and its answer, which the worker writes: follow it by its id.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: One for each file, in their order: the folders below `folder_id` it goes into, such as `Invoices/2024`, made where none of their name is, or empty for that folder itself.

Chat.title: Chat
Chat.description:
A chat with the agent: private to the member who started it until they share it with the
project, whose members then read it; only its starter asks in it.

ChatChange.title: ChatChange
ChatChange.description:
A chat renamed, shared with the project or taken private again; a field left out stays as
it is.

ChatList.title: ChatList
ChatList.description:
A page of the chats of a project the key's member started or that were shared with it,
the newest first.

CheckRun.title: CheckRun
CheckRun.description:
A run of a project's cross-checks. `status` is `queued` or `running` until it is worked
out, then `done` or `failed`; `report_status` is the discrepancy report's, None when none was
asked for. The report cites the passages of `report_sources` as [P<id>].

CheckRunEvent.title: CheckRunEvent
CheckRunEvent.description:
A run of a project's cross-checks worked out, or failed, and its discrepancy report
written or failed when one was asked for, posted to the organisation's webhooks that listen
for it. A report asked for after the run is announced again once it is written. `id` names
the event, the same in every try of it.

CheckRunList.title: CheckRunList
CheckRunList.description: A page of a project's runs, the newest first.

CrossCheck.title: CrossCheck
CrossCheck.description:
A rule a project's documents are checked against one another by, and why it cannot be
worked out with the project's templates as they are now, if it cannot.

Document.title: Document
Document.description:
A document and how far it is indexed. `status` is `queued` or `processing` while it is
read, `ready` once it can be searched and asked about, `failed` when it could not be read and
`quarantined` when the malware scan flagged it, `error` saying why. A ready document is
`partly_indexed` when it went without summaries and facts or without the vectors that search
by meaning, which the model or the embeddings being out causes; `retry_at` is when a stage
that failed for a reason that passes runs again by itself.

DocumentChange.title: DocumentChange
DocumentChange.description:
A document renamed, moved or both; a field left out stays as it is, and a `folder_id` of
null moves it to the root. A new name keeps the file's extension.

DocumentEvent.title: DocumentEvent
DocumentEvent.description:
A document's indexing ended, posted to the organisation's webhooks that listen for it:
`document.ready` once it can be searched and asked about (`data.partly_indexed` says whether
it went without a part), `document.failed` once it could not be read or was quarantined
(`data.error` says why). `id` names the event, the same in every try of it.

DocumentList.title: DocumentList
DocumentList.description: A page of a project's documents, the newest first.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
A refusal: what was refused and what to do next, in a sentence for the person the program
works for.

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description:
A fact read from a document: a field's value as written, typed as a number, a date or an
amount with its currency where it is one, with the words it was read from and where they are.
`verified` says the words were found in the text; `check` is a member's word on it.

FactCheck.title: FactCheck
FactCheck.description:
A member's check of a fact: who and when, the model's value when they corrected it, and
what they said the document states.

FactList.title: FactList
FactList.description: A page of facts, the oldest first.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description:
What a rule of a run found for a value of a document: whether it differs, is missing or
holds, and why; the fact checked and those it was compared with, as they were read when the
run was made; the documents paired with it; and the checked value less the other (or their
sum), in days for dates.

FindingList.title: FindingList
FindingList.description:
A page of what one rule of a run found, differing first, then missing, then holding, and
how many of the outcome asked for (or of all) it found.

Folder.title: Folder
Folder.description:
A folder of a project's library, with its path from the root and how many documents it
holds itself, not counting its folders'.

FolderChange.title: FolderChange
FolderChange.description:
A folder renamed, moved or both; a field left out stays as it is, and a `parent_id` of
null moves it to the root.

FolderList.title: FolderList
FolderList.description: A project's folders, the oldest first; a tree is built from `parent_id`.

Message.title: Message
Message.description:
A question, or the agent's answer. While an answer's `status` is `streaming` it is being
written and `content` is what was written so far; it ends `done`, `stopped` or `failed`,
`error` saying why. `notice` is what the answer adds about itself, such as that it stopped.

MessageList.title: MessageList
MessageList.description: A page of a chat's questions and answers, the oldest first.

NewCheckRun.title: NewCheckRun
NewCheckRun.description:
A run of the project's cross-checks, those named or all of them, and whether the agent
writes a discrepancy report once they are worked out, which counts as a question.

NewFolder.title: NewFolder
NewFolder.description: A folder to make, at the project's root or in another of its folders.

NewProject.title: NewProject
NewProject.description:
A project to make: one the organisation sees, or one private to the key's member, and the
organisation's owners and admins, until they choose others in the app.

Passage.title: Passage
Passage.description:
A passage of a document, as an answer cites it ([P<id>]): the section it is in, its text
and its pages.

PlanError.title: PlanError
PlanError.description:
A refusal by the organisation's plan, with the figure it was held to; never answered since
the app has no plans.

Project.title: Project
Project.description:
A project: its documents are searched and asked about together. The sample project a new
organisation starts with takes no uploads.

ProjectChange.title: ProjectChange
ProjectChange.description: A project renamed or described anew; a field left out stays as it is.

ProjectList.title: ProjectList
ProjectList.description: The projects the key's member sees, the newest first.

content.title: Content
examples: Does the invoice match the contract's prices?

RejectedFile.title: RejectedFile
RejectedFile.description:
A file of an upload that was not kept, by its place among the files sent (from 0) and its
name, and why: a sentence, `limit` always null since the app has no plans, and the document
that holds the same bytes when the project holds them already, which is no failure.

Rule.title: Rule
Rule.description:
A rule of a run as it was when the run was made, by its place in the run (`rule` of its
findings), the cross-check's id and name, and once the run is worked out why it could not be
or what it found.

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description: A passage that matched, with the words around the match, and how well it matched.

SearchResults.title: SearchResults
SearchResults.description:
The passages that match best, the best first; `semantic` is false while search matches
keywords alone.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Whether a part of the service can be used just now, and if not, what cannot be done.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: A passage the agent was shown, which its answer cites as [P<passage_id>].

Status.title: Status
Status.description:
What the deployment can do just now: answer questions and read summaries and facts
(`models`), search by meaning as well as by keywords (`search`), and index uploads and write
answers at all (`workers`); and what one upload may carry.

Upload.title: Upload
Upload.description:
The documents an upload kept, in the order their files were sent, and the files it did
not. Each document is indexed in the background: follow it by its id.

UploadLimits.title: UploadLimits
UploadLimits.description:
What one upload may carry: how many files, how many bytes together and each, and the file
types the app reads, by their extensions.

Version.title: Version
Version.description:
A version of a document: its current file, or an earlier one, kept to download, whose text
nothing searches or answers from any more.

VersionList.title: VersionList
VersionList.description:
A document's versions, the current one first, then the earlier ones, the latest first: every
one of them, on one page.

APIKey.description: An API key, which an owner or admin of the organisation makes on its page, sent as `Authorization: Bearer emk_…`. It acts as the member who made it, in the organisation's projects alone, reading or reading and changing as it was made.

tags.name: status
tags.description: What the deployment can do just now, and what one upload may carry.

tags.name: projects
tags.description: The organisation's projects that the key's member sees, each with documents that are searched and asked about together.

tags.name: folders
tags.description: The folders a project's library keeps its documents in.

tags.name: documents
tags.description: Files uploaded into a project, each indexed in the background before it is searched and asked about.

tags.name: facts
tags.description: The values read from documents by the project's extraction templates, each with the words it was read from.

tags.name: search
tags.description: The passages of a project's documents, found by keywords and by meaning.

tags.name: chats
tags.description: Questions asked about a project's documents, and the answers the agent writes, followed as they are written.

tags.name: cross-checks
tags.description: The rules a project's documents are checked against one another by, which members write in the app; 404 for an organisation that does not have them yet.

tags.name: check-runs
tags.description: Runs of a project's cross-checks, what each rule found and the discrepancy report; 404 for an organisation that does not have them yet.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: The events posted to the organisation's webhooks as they happen, which owners and admins add on its page.
